findings.text: §25 item 1 ("`call_decisions()` and `acall_decisions()` go in `imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py`, beside `call_llm_structured()`, as the one canonical route to a decisions model") proposes machinery already present at HEAD; every element it lists has landed, in the exact shape §25 specifies. Instances of this defect across §25's `decisions-call` node (plan line 390) and design item 1 (plan lines 353–366): `call_decisions` (`imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3429`), `acall_decisions` (`imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3493`), the shared title-header helper `_service_headers` (`imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:1995`, already called from `_build_kwargs` at `:2008`), `DECISIONS_ENDPOINT` and the retry/validation helpers (`imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3249`, `:3276`, `:3289`), the `discovery-relevance` seat (`imas_codex/settings.py:148` in `MODEL_SECTIONS`, `:180` default `typesafe/jev-1.13`, `pyproject.toml:402`), and the node's own test file `tests/discovery/test_llm_decisions.py`. All are contained in commit `3e91ac114` ("feat(discovery): add typed decisions call layer and Jev seat"), which `git merge-base --is-ancestor 3e91ac114 HEAD` confirms is an ancestor of the worktree base. The plan still lists §25 as `implementable` (`plan-section-declarations` → `s25`) with `decisions-call` as a to-do node, so a worker dispatched to it will either rebuild existing code or discover it is already done mid-node — the plan record and the code disagree.

findings.text: the `decisions-call` node's declared write of `imas_codex/settings.py` (adding the seat to `MODEL_SECTIONS` and, "if it takes an environment override, `_MODEL_ENV_VARS`") is already complete: `imas_codex/settings.py:144` lists `discovery-relevance` in `MODEL_SECTIONS`, `:219` lists `IMAS_CODEX_DISCOVERY_RELEVANCE_MODEL` in the env-var map, and `:180` carries the model. A worker following the brief as written would re-edit the settings owners the seat already lives in — the same stale-node defect as the finding above, but on the settings file rather than the call layer, and named so a scope-holder can retire the node rather than re-trial it.
